layout_map: Near-black space backdrop with a faint cyan grid texture across the full frame. A single glowing cosmic-web object (a speckled blue/violet sphere of galactic filaments) is dead-center, ~x640 y360, filling cells 6-7-10-11 and spanning roughly x480-x800, y130-y480. A short white caption sits along the bottom-center, baseline ~y560, small all-caps reading 'IT'S EXPANDING FAST AND GETTING FASTER' across cells 14-15. No headline text, no number badge — the hero glowing object carries the whole frame.
reads_as: a lone glowing cosmic structure pulsing in dark space — what IS that?
why_it_works: single luminous object on near-black void maximizes contrast and isolation; the lone glow forces the eye to it and poses a silent mystery.
mimic_for: a single mysterious phenomenon or object is the whole story and you want it isolated and glowing on dark void
title: How Will The Universe Die?

layout_map: A 16:9 frame whose center band (~x430-850) holds a vertical Shorts still of the host (Cleo) framed shoulders-up, face center ~x640 y300 occupying cells 6-7-10-11, filling roughly the middle third of the width. She looks intent toward camera with a slightly open, animated mouth (mid-talk reaction). Her right hand is raised and pointing/gesturing at lower-center, ~x640 y430 (cell 11), drawing the eye. The outer thirds (cells 1-5-9-13 and 4-8-12-16) are a darkened, blurred duplicate of the same still acting as letterbox wings. No headline overlay; a tiny faint caption sits at bottom-center ~y460. The host's expressive face plus the pointing hand are the entire scroll-stop.
reads_as: the host caught mid-explanation, pointing — she's about to show you something insane
why_it_works: an animated talking-head face with a directional hand gesture creates parasocial urgency and points the eye toward the payoff; no text needed because the expression IS the hook.
mimic_for: a personality-driven reveal where the host's live reaction and a pointing gesture sell the moment more than any headline
title: Jupiter’s Moons Are Insane

layout_map: A 16:9 frame with a deep blue-to-navy underwater gradient backdrop (darkened blurred wings on the outer thirds, cells 1/5/9/13 and 4/8/12/16). Center band holds an illustrated freediver descending head-first, body running top-to-bottom through cells 3-7-11, head/face at the bottom ~x640 y480 (cell 11), green-finned feet up top at ~y40. The diver's chest shows two red illustrated lungs (danger cue) at ~x640 y380. Left of the diver, a vertical depth/air gauge runs down cell 2-6-10 (~x520) with a bright ORANGE fill pill ending in a white ':23' countdown badge at ~x530 y460. A duplicate large ghosted ':23' sits in the bottom-left corner ~x290 y670. Small white caption 'I'M RUNNING OUT OF AIR' centered baseline ~y560.
reads_as: a diver plunging deeper with a ticking :23 timer and red lungs — they're running out of air
why_it_works: the orange progress/air bar plus a literal countdown number injects time-pressure jeopardy; the red lungs and downward dive direction make the stakes visceral.
mimic_for: a countdown / time-running-out / depleting-resource jeopardy beat where a progress bar and a ticking number raise the stakes
title: What If You Were A Whale?

layout_map: Near-black deep-sea backdrop; the center band (~x430-850) is a slightly lighter blue-grey shaft of light with darkened blurred wings on the outer thirds. A pale, ghostly cyan-lit giant squid hangs vertically dead-center, mantle/tip at ~x640 y90 and tentacles fanning out around ~x640 y330 (cells 7-11), body spanning roughly y40-y420. A tiny 'SOURCE: DISCOVERY' credit sits top-center ~x600 y45. Small white caption 'THIS IS THE FIRST EVER...' centered baseline ~y560. The faint glowing creature emerging from pitch black is the entire frame — no headline, no number.
reads_as: a ghostly giant squid floating up out of the black abyss — real, rare footage
why_it_works: an eerie luminous creature isolated against near-total darkness exploits curiosity about the rare and the deep; the 'first ever' caption promises something never-seen.
mimic_for: a rare never-before-seen object or creature revealed against darkness, where the subject's strangeness alone stops the scroll
title: The First Ever Footage of a Giant Squid

layout_map: Full-bleed cutaway of the sun's interior: glowing orange-to-yellow molten layers arc across the lower two-thirds (cells 9-16), with concentric red/orange shells. The top strip (cells 1-4) is dark near-black space. A bold white headline badge '2 MILLION °C' sits top-center, baseline ~y45, across cells 2-3 (~x420-720). A thin white curved arrow drops from the text down-right into the hot layer, tip at ~x690 y95 (cell 7), pointing at the searing core region. A faint small caption sits centered ~y150. The giant temperature stat plus the pointing arrow into the glowing core carry the frame.
reads_as: the sun cut open glowing orange, labeled 2 MILLION °C — staggering heat made literal
why_it_works: a shocking concrete number paired with an arrow physically connecting it to the glowing hot region turns an abstract stat into a visceral 'that's insane' reaction.
mimic_for: a jaw-dropping magnitude stat (temperature, speed, size) that you want to pin with an arrow onto the glowing/cutaway object it describes
title: What’s Really Inside The Sun?

layout_map: 16:9 frame, center band (~x430-850) a vertical Shorts still of the host in a warm-lit room with plants; darkened blurred duplicate wings fill the outer thirds. Cleo is framed chest-up, face center ~x640 y210 (cells 6-7), looking down toward her hands. She holds a small blue Earth globe in her cupped hands at center, ~x640 y370 (cell 11), the globe glowing slightly and drawing the eye to the lower-center. A faint small caption sits centered ~y450. No headline overlay — the host presenting/cradling the globe object is the whole composition.
reads_as: the host holding a tiny glowing Earth in her hands — intimate, she's about to explain something about our planet
why_it_works: a human holding a miniature of the subject creates scale-play and a hand-prop focal point; the warm domestic setting plus eye-line down to the globe feels personal and curiosity-baiting.
mimic_for: the host literally holding/presenting a miniature of the subject as a hand-prop, making an abstract planetary topic intimate and tangible
title: Can Earth Get Rings Like Saturn?

layout_map: 16:9 frame, center band (~x430-850) holds a vertical three-row stacked comparison; darkened blurred wings on the outer thirds. Top row (cells 3-7, y0-240) a snow-capped peak photo labeled 'MAUNA KEA' in green/lime pixelated all-caps, baseline ~y95. Middle row (y240-440) a broad shield-volcano slope landscape labeled 'MAUNA LOA' in the same lime pixel caps, baseline ~y290. Bottom row (y440-720) ocean with a small rocky islet labeled 'GARDNER PINNACLE' (two lines) in lime caps, baseline ~y480/y510. Small white caption 'YOU DECIDE THE WINNER.' centered ~y560. Three stacked candidates each tagged, no single hero.
reads_as: three mountains stacked and labeled in green — which is the biggest, you decide
why_it_works: a vertical stacked ranking of labeled candidates invites comparison and a 'you pick' engagement loop; the consistent lime pixel labels read as a game/tier list.
mimic_for: a head-to-head ranking of three labeled candidates stacked vertically where the viewer is invited to judge the winner
title: How Big is the Biggest Volcano?

layout_map: Near-black starfield backdrop with a faint cyan grid. Two planets stacked vertically dead-center: a cratered tan/orange Venus up top at ~x680 y100 (cell 7, ~x560-820 wide), and a blue-and-white Earth directly below at ~x640 y320 (cell 11), the two roughly the same size to invite a like-for-like size read. A small white caption 'AND IT'S ABOUT THE SAME SIZE' sits centered baseline ~y440 (cell 11/15). No headline, no number — the two same-size planets paired on dark space carry the comparison.
reads_as: Venus over Earth, side-by-side same size — wait, are they twins?
why_it_works: two planets matched in scale on black space sets up an implicit comparison ('about the same size') that primes the surprise; the dark void keeps the pair clean and high-contrast.
mimic_for: an apples-to-apples size/scale comparison of two celestial or round objects stacked on dark space to make their similarity or difference pop
title: Is There Life on Venus?
